entries.name: Preston King

expected.sentence:
Refused to submit to a draft physical after the Georgia draft board addressed him by first name rather than 'Mr.' Arrested in 1960, convicted of draft evasion by an all-white jury and sentenced to 18 months. Broke bail and lived in exile abroad for decades rather than serve.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — found guilty by an all-white jury in 1960; later pardoned in 2000

updates.sentence:
Refused to submit to a draft physical after the Georgia draft board addressed him by first name rather than 'Mr.' Arrested in 1960, convicted of draft evasion by an all-white jury and sentenced to 18 months. Broke bail and lived in exile abroad for decades rather than serve.

Verdict as recorded: Yes — found guilty by an all-white jury in April 1961; later pardoned in 2000

Arrested in December 1960 and released on bail. Sentenced in April 1961; he did not serve the eighteen-month sentence. He left the United States in 1961 and returned on February 23, 2000, after receiving a presidential pardon on February 21. Exact initial detention and departure dates remain unverified.
